top.text: A thousand games, respect. One trick that helps: sort the pile by how long each game takes to finish and clear the short ones first, so the number drops fast.

Access years from now is the one that price can't fix later. DRM-free games, like the ones on GOG, cover a lot of it: you keep the installer, it plays offline, and it doesn't depend on a launcher or an account.
Fair question, it's a huge install. Check the Steam Deck compatibility badge on the store page and your free storage first, and an SD card helps if the internal drive is tight.
Capping is worth it. Setting it at or just below your monitor’s refresh rate keeps the PC cooler and quieter, and frame pacing often feels smoother.
Trying the class you’re curious about first is a fair way to call it. That way you quit knowing exactly what you tried.
